title: How Much Does a Michelin Star Restaurant Cost? (2026 Prices)
description: What a Michelin star restaurant costs at one, two and three stars and country by country: dinner, lunch and wine pairings, plus service, tax and tips.
h1: How Much Does a Michelin Star Restaurant Cost?
summary: Typical prices at one, two and three stars and in every country we cover, with wine pairings, service, tax and tips added up.
keywords: how much does a michelin star restaurant cost
how much is a michelin star meal
how much is a 3 star michelin restaurant
how expensive are michelin star restaurants
how much to tip at michelin star restaurant
body:
A Michelin star restaurant typically costs {{price1}} per person for a one-star dinner tasting menu, {{price2}} at two stars and {{price3}} at three, before drinks and service. Add a wine pairing and the service, tax or tip usually charged, and a typical three-star dinner comes to {{costTotal3}} a head.

Those are medians from the published prices of {{costMenus}} Michelin-starred restaurants in {{costCountries}} countries, out of the {{total}} on The Starred Bill, converted to US dollars at recent exchange rates. Below is what a starred meal costs at each level, what lunch and a wine pairing add, how prices compare from country to country, what service, tax and tips do to the bill, and the most expensive menus in the world. Prices last checked {{checked}}.

How much is a Michelin star meal?

Each extra star costs more, but not in equal steps. A typical one-star dinner menu costs {{price1}}, and most fall between {{range1}}. A second star takes the typical price to {{price2}}, and a third to {{price3}}, a little over twice the one-star figure. The range inside each level is wide: {{costUnder100_1}} one-star restaurants serve a dinner menu for $100 or less, while a handful of one-star sushi counters charge more than most three-star dining rooms.

{{table:cost-stars}}

The last column is the figure most price guides leave out: the whole evening. Take each restaurant’s dinner menu and its wine pairing, add what is usually charged on top in its country, and the typical bill comes to {{costTotal1}} a person at one star, {{costTotal2}} at two and {{costTotal3}} at three. For two people, a three-star dinner with wine typically costs {{costTwo3}}. A wine pairing typically adds {{costWineShare1}} to the menu price at one star, and about as much at two and three, so it is the biggest single choice you make after picking the restaurant.

How much is a 3-star Michelin restaurant?

A dinner tasting menu at a three-Michelin-star restaurant typically costs {{price3}} per person before drinks and service, and most of the world’s {{n3}} three-star restaurants charge between {{range3}}. The cheapest three-star dinner menu we list is {{costCheap3Price}} at {{costCheap3Name}} in {{costCheap3Place}}, and the most expensive is {{costDear3Price}} at {{costDear3Name}} in {{costDear3Place}}. Lunch brings it down: where a three-star restaurant serves a set lunch, it typically costs {{lunch3}}. Every one of them, with its price, is in our list of all the three-Michelin-star restaurants in the world.

Here is what a three-star dinner with the wine pairing comes to in seven cities, once each country’s usual service, tax or tip is added:

{{table:cost-examples}}

Two menus at similar prices can end very differently. In New York, sales tax and a tip of about 20% add almost a third to the bill; in Paris and Copenhagen, service is already in the menu price, and Danish prices include 25% VAT too. That is why our destination pages show each restaurant’s prices as a till receipt with the local service line on it.

Michelin star restaurant prices by country

Where you eat matters almost as much as how many stars. Among the {{costBigCountries}} countries where 20 or more starred restaurants publish a dinner menu price, {{costDearCountry}} is the most expensive, with a typical dinner menu of {{costDearCountryPrice}}, and {{costCheapCountry}} the cheapest, at {{costCheapCountryPrice}}. Big cities cost more than the countryside: a typical starred dinner menu costs {{costDinner_paris}} in Paris against {{costDinner_france}} across France as a whole, where hundreds of starred restaurants sit in small towns and villages. In the United States, prices look middling in the table but come before sales tax and tip. For local prices, our pages for Copenhagen, New York and London list every starred restaurant’s dinner, lunch and wine pairing price.

{{table:cost-countries}}

Service, tax and tips: what is added to the bill

A menu price is rarely the whole bill. Depending on the country, service, sales tax or a tip can add nothing at all or nearly a third, and the same menu price can mean a very different evening in Tokyo and in Toronto. Our prices are always the menu price as the restaurant lists it, and this is what usually comes on top:

{{table:cost-service}}

How much to tip at a Michelin star restaurant

It depends on the country. In the United States and Canada, a tip of 18–22% of the bill before tax is the norm at starred restaurants, unless the restaurant adds a service charge or says service is included, as some now do, so read the bill before you tip. On a typical American one-star dinner menu of {{costDinner1_usa}}, a 20% tip adds about {{costTip1_usa}} a person before drinks. In the UK and Ireland, the 12.5% service charge on the bill is the tip, and in Singapore and Bangkok the “++” service charge is too. Across most of Europe, in South Korea and in Japan, service is part of the price and no tip is expected, though rounding up after a memorable evening is welcome outside Japan.

How expensive are Michelin star restaurants?

Are Michelin star restaurants expensive? Mostly yes, but not all of them. A starred dinner menu costs more than most nights out anywhere, and {{costOver300}} of the {{costMenus}} starred restaurants that publish one ({{costShareOver300}}) charge more than $300 a head before drinks. But a star rates the cooking, not the luxury, so the bottom of the range is surprisingly low: {{cheapUnder50}} starred restaurants serve a meal for about $50 or less, from noodle counters in Hong Kong to hawker stalls in Singapore, where a starred bowl costs from about {{cheapUSD}}. Our guide to the cheapest Michelin star meals in the world ranks them all.

Why are Michelin star restaurants so expensive?

Mostly because of people. A starred kitchen has a large brigade of cooks, and the dining room its own team of servers and sommeliers, often for just a few dozen guests a night. Many menus run to ten courses or more, each prepared to order, with produce bought from small farms, day boats and specialist suppliers at prices well above wholesale. Rent in the city centers where most starred restaurants sit adds the rest. A star then adds demand: once a restaurant is fully booked weeks ahead, it has little reason to charge less. The MICHELIN Guide itself pays no attention to price when it awards stars, which is why its Bib Gourmand, its award for good cooking at moderate prices, sits beside the stars.

The most expensive Michelin star restaurants

The most expensive Michelin star restaurant on our list is {{costTopName}} in {{costTopPlace}}, a {{costTopStars}}-star restaurant whose dinner costs {{costTopPrice}} per person before drinks and service. Stars and price don’t line up neatly at the top: only {{costTop3Count}} of the 10 most expensive dinner menus are at three-star restaurants. Sushi counters with a handful of seats and remote destination restaurants that cook only for a few guests a night can charge more than the grandest three-star dining rooms.

{{table:cost-top}}

How to pay less for a Michelin star meal

  • Go at lunch. Of the {{lunchBoth}} starred restaurants that list both a set lunch and a set dinner menu, {{lunchCheaper}} ({{lunchShare}}) charge less at lunch, and where they do, lunch typically costs about half the dinner price.
  • Start with one star. A typical one-star dinner menu costs less than half a three-star one, and a one-star set lunch typically costs {{lunch1}}.
  • Choose the wine yourself. A pairing adds more than half the menu price again; a bottle shared at the table or a glass or two often costs less.
  • Pick your country. The cheapest countries with 20 or more priced starred restaurants are {{costCheapCountries}}, where a typical dinner menu costs well under $200.
  • Know what is included. A $200 menu in New York comes to about $260 once tax and tip are added, while a €210 menu in Paris is the whole bill, so compare whole bills. Our Compare page puts two or three restaurants from your wishlist side by side in one currency.

To find a restaurant that fits a set budget, Help me pick asks six quick questions and suggests three, with the whole bill worked out.

How we worked out these prices

Every figure on this page is worked out from the restaurant data behind The Starred Bill each time the site is rebuilt, so it stays current as prices and stars change. Stars come from the current MICHELIN Guide editions ({{guideYear}} or the latest before each). Prices come from each restaurant’s own website where it publishes them, else from recent reviews and booking sites, and each one is listed with its source on our destination pages. “Typical” means the median: half the restaurants charge more and half less. We count the main dinner tasting menu, per person, as the restaurant lists it; à la carte prices, single dishes and the typical spends that most of mainland China’s restaurants are listed with are left out. Wine pairings are the restaurant’s own pairing for that menu. US dollar figures use recent exchange rates, so they move a little with currencies.

Journalists, bloggers and researchers are welcome to quote these figures. Please credit The Starred Bill and link to this page.

faq.q: Do you have to order the tasting menu at a Michelin star restaurant?
faq.a: Not always. Many one-star restaurants also serve à la carte or a shorter menu, and our destination pages note a restaurant’s other menus where it lists them. At most two- and three-star restaurants the tasting menu is the only choice at dinner, and the whole table usually has to order the same one.

faq.q: Do Michelin star restaurants charge a deposit or a cancellation fee?
faq.a: Often. Many starred restaurants take card details or a prepaid ticket when you book, through systems like Tock, Resy or OpenTable, and charge part or all of the menu price if you cancel late or don’t turn up. At the most sought-after restaurants the whole meal is paid in advance, so check the cancellation terms before you book.
